newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge defers ruling in Brown case.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge defers ruling in Brown case.

text.p: Florida Judge Brian Davis heard arguments but did not rule Tuesday on a motion by Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp to overturn a jury award of $750,000 to a smoker with lung cancer.

Lawyers for Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, argued Tuesday before Davis in Duval County Circuit Court that the judge had erred in allowing company documents to be presented as evidence in an earlier trial.

A six-member circuit jury had ruled on August 9 that Brown & Williamson was negligent and made a dangerous and defective product in the case of Grady Carter of Orange Park, Fla., who smoked for 50 years until he was diagnosed with lung cancer.
The ruling would be appealed to a higher court if Davis rejected the motion for a new trial or a direct verdict, for which the tobacco company's attorneys argued Tuesday.
